headline: Funding flows. Budgets stall. Innovation lingers.
deck: This week saw mixed signals with funding surges and budget stagnation.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense pull
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190M in a Series C round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding highlights the growing demand for co-orbital security solutions, especially as the DoD emphasizes space domain awareness. With the defense sector's appetite for innovative security solutions, True Anomaly is well-positioned to capitalize.
stories.soWhat: It's a reminder that in defense, cash often flows more freely than actual innovation.

stories.head: Iridium's acquisition of Aireon raises eyebrows
stories.body: Iridium is acquiring the remaining stake in Aireon for an undisclosed amount, aiming to enhance its aviation safety services. This move is akin to adding lifeguards to a crowded pool, as Iridium already has a solid footing in satellite communications. The integration could streamline operations, but the real question is whether it will effectively address the market's growing safety demands.
stories.soWhat: In a saturated market, simply expanding services may not guarantee success.

stories.head: NASA's flat budget reflects stagnation
stories.body: The House Appropriations Committee has approved a spending bill that keeps NASA's budget flat, a move that could hinder ambitious projects. With no increase in funding, NASA may struggle to meet its long-term goals, especially as competitors ramp up their own space initiatives. This stagnation could stifle innovation at a time when the industry needs it most.
stories.soWhat: In space, a flat budget is often the first step toward a downward spiral.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on AST SpaceMobile's launch plans
watchlist.body: The potential use of ULA's Vulcan rocket could diversify AST SpaceMobile's launch options, impacting its timeline and costs.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension implications
watchlist.body: The $480M extension on the TITAN program could signal increased demand for ground station capabilities in a data-driven defense landscape.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser developments
watchlist.body: With the Dream Chaser DoD variant clearing its design review, its future missions could reshape logistics in space.

watchlist.title: Watch for hypersonic test delays
watchlist.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests could signal deeper issues in defense project management and execution.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
